recs.name: Heart of the Cliffs
recs.tag: 'The climb is easy; the descent is hard.'

lines.x: Hmm...
That crevice over there should be close enough...
Weiss, how long do you think it'll be before my brother comes back?
Based on what the Master said before the trip, about three or four more days.
Eh... That's still pretty far from now.
Huh? Is that him...?
No wait, is it my sister?!
The Saintess went to the Vine-Bead Court months ago. With everything she must attend to, there's no way she'd be here. No need to get antsy; I'll get the door.
Oh, Auntie Tarja! What brings you here?
Okay!
That's one step closer!
The cave's not really all that high up, so I should be there soon.
Tearstone?
It's a kind of light blue ore, only found in a cave halfway up Mount Karlan. Legend has it that it's the condensed tears of Kjeragandr.
Almost there!
So Uncle Tarja's condition got worse, the tearstone that was supposed to last over half a year was used up by autumn, and no one on either side of the mountain can lend him any more?
How could this happen...?
According to legend, tearstone can only be mined one palmful at a time, for that is the size of one of Kjeragandr's teardrops.
If any more are extracted at once, then they lose their effectiveness.
In fact, you were the one who retrieved the one Mister Tarja was using. That was two years ago though, so you might not remember it.
Oh, right, I remember now!
Weiss, think you could bring Auntie Tarja with you and drive around to see if anyone else has any tearstone?
Milady, you...
I'll keep looking around the house. I remember picking up a little one to use as a decoration, but can't remember where I put it.
Are you sure?
Y-Yeah, I'm positive. As soon as I find it, I'll grind it down for Uncle Tarja and decoct it.
And if you do manage to find one, you don't need to come tell me. Just head straight to the Tarja household.
Please be careful, milady.
It's... It's not like I'll be doing anything dangerous, just looking around the house! Anyway, get going already! Someone's life is on the line here!
Alright.
I'll get the car ready. Missus Tarja, come with me.
Ensia turns her head and takes a look at the ashen-gray sky.
For now, the clouds aren't too dense, and not even a single sign of wind can be seen through the window.
Weiss's intuition is as sharp as ever.
If it weren't for Uncle Tarja's emergency situation, he definitely wouldn't have left me alone.
Seriously, he's way too much of a worrywart. The snow won't be coming down hard until later in the evening anyway, and the cave isn't too high up. Just a quick climb up the cliff.
Welp, up we go!
Now all that's left is to head in and mine some tearstone. Shouldn't take long!
Ensia closes her eyes and silently bows to the holy Mount Karlan.
Success! Fits perfectly, right inside my palm.
Still, I may have been pulling a fast one on Weiss, but tearstones are so pretty. Maybe I really should grab a few more for decoration next time...
That said, I can still see the marks I made on the walls here two years ago. Nothing's changed at all.
Ensia stands at the mouth of the cave and looks down the mountain. She can still see the smoke from the Tarja household.
Just wait for me. I'll get you your tearstone in no time flat!
Brrr, so cold!
The wind's kicking up?!
Crap, that snowstorm's coming in a lot sooner than I thought.
Welp, can't get down the cliff anymore. Better take shelter in the cave and wait it out...
Wait, no. Uncle Tarja's still waiting for that tearstone, and who knows when the storm will stop?
I'll have to descend from the other side then.
Hmm... This route seems usable, but which way am I...?
This tree looks familiar... Wait, haven't I been here already?
I'll make a sign with my climbing rope. At least that way I won't be going in circles.
This path is... going in the exact wrong direction.
Ugh, this snow couldn't have come at a worse time.
I think I've come a pretty long way...
The cave is on the side of the mountain where it meets the lake, but I've been heading towards the lake this entire time...
I guess I'm already trespassing on Paleroche land then.
Stepping into another clan's territory without notice...
Even though her brother never went out of his way to discuss the other two clans with her, Ensia is no fool.
She knows that the Paleroche and Silverash clans have been at odds ever since Enciodes returned to Kjerag.
And before his latest trip, he specifically warned her not to have anything to do with the Paleroches unless absolutely necessary.
The situation in Kjerag was too delicate, and even a single careless whisper could trigger an avalanche.
Maybe I should turn back before they find me. Wait out the snow before heading back down...
No, I can't risk it. Doesn't look like it'll be stopping anytime soon.
This is a matter of life and death here! Time is of the essence!
At least the snow's thick enough that I didn't get hurt by the fall...
Hmm, I can see the settlements at the foot of the mountain.
And the lake too.
Feels like I've been trekking through the mountain's backside for forever. How is there still more trail...?
I can't even see the lake anymore...
I can tell I'm still descending, but this trail is way too long—
Suddenly a figure emerges through the wind and snow and into Ensia's field of view, like a miracle.
Hello? Hello?!
Can you hear me? I'm over here! Over here!
The figure notices her immediately and walks straight towards her.
Thank Kjeragandr! Are you a hunter from the mountains? How far are we from the bottom?
If you follow this trail down, you'll be off the mountain in about an hour and a half.
An hour and a half? Still that far?
There wouldn't happen to be any shortcuts?
There are, but none that can be used in a snowstorm this fierce.
I have mountaineering equipment! See this big ole backpack? I've got an icepick, climbing ropes, rock nails, the whole shebang!
Hmm... It could be worth a try then.
If you head back a bit to where you just saw the lake, there's a steep little trail covered in snow.
Thank you! By the way, I didn't get your...
Before Ensia could finish her words, there was nothing in her field of view except the wind and snow. As if Kjeragandr had deliberately hidden her guide from her.
She's gone?!
Well, whatever. Let's head back and give this a shot!
It worked!
That must've saved at least half an hour! Now to find a place where I can rent a burdenbeast or—
Stop! Who goes there?
Hello, I don't mean any harm! I'm...
Huh? Aren't you the second daughter of the Silverash clan?
I can explain, I—
Hmph, I'm just patrol the mountain. Save your explanation for the head of our clan!
The fragrance of the hot tea and sweets prepared by the servants still wafts from the table, but the two in the reception room do not sit, nor does a single drop or crumb pass their lips.
Tell me, what's going on here?
I'm sorry! I didn't mean to trespass into your territory!
Everyone who gets caught says that.
I mean it though...
So you're telling me you were taking a walk in your backyard, enjoying the snow, and just happened to end up near the lake?

No, I went to mine tearstone from a mountain cave, and it started snowing right as I was about to leave. Since I couldn't get down the cliff near my house, I headed the opposite direction, towards the lake.
Did you not see the dark clouds? You chose now of all times to mine your tearstone?
I’ve heard enough.
No, Mister Arctosz, let me explain—
The second daughter of the Silverash clan has trespassed on Paleroche territory.
I'll have your brother explain the situation once he returns. If his answer satisfies me, I'll let you go.
(He's going to wait for Enciodes?!)
(But Uncle Tarja is sick and can't wait any longer!)
(I need to get this medicine to him right away! Which means my only choice is to—)
(But now that it's come to this, I don't know what Mister Arctosz's demands will be, or if my brother will be humiliated...)
(Damn it, none of this has anything to do with the clans! Just because I'm a Silverash...)
(I'm sorry, Enciodes! If this causes any trouble, I'll make it right, I swear!)
Judging by the look on your face, it seems you have something to say.
I sincerely apologize for trespassing into the lake area, and I'll accept however you choose to handle this matter.
But I went to mine tearstone in order to save someone's life...
Using another's life as an excuse is an awfully tasteless joke, Ensia Silverash.
I'm not lying! Uncle Tarja, who lives in the mountains, is seriously ill and needs a tearstone to save his life. That's why I went up there!

I'll accept whatever punishment you have for me, but I ask only that you send an express train to deliver the tearstone in my backpack to the Tarja household in the mountains. Please, I'm begging you!
If you claim to have mined tearstone, then show it to me.
Hmm... this is certainly tearstone. But isn't it a bit too big?
While I was up there, I made sure to test if it could fit in the palm of my hand.
At least SOME of the Silverashes still remember a few of Kjeragandr's old teachings.
And you want me to deliver this to the Tarja household in the mountains, correct?
Yes!
Hmph.
I suppose I can oblige.
Prepare the swiftest burdenbeast! I'll be heading to the mountains with Ensia Silverash!
(Thank goodness...)
(—Wait, back up, with ME?!)
Mister Arctosz, do you mean to say...
If the situation is as you described, then your trespass was truly unintentional.
Paleroche has no desire to raise a fuss over something like this.
I thought you would—
Would what?
N-nothing, nothing at all!
Thank goodness...
You have my deepest gratitude, Mister Arctosz! If we waited any longer, we might've been too late! Truly, I can't thank you enough!
You harvested the tearstone. It was your life to save. There's nothing to thank me for.
No, you deserve it! Would you like to stop by my house to rest for a bit? Uncle Matterhorn should be back shortly, and maybe I can let him—
Arctosz doesn't utter a word, simply gazing down at the excited Ensia like an immovable crag.
Sorry, I'm getting way ahead of myself.
Don't worry about it.
Mister Arctosz...
Did you need anything else?
I still remember back before Enciodes returned. You were never close to me or my sister, but you didn't keep your distance from us like you do now.

If anyone's responsible for that, it would be your dear old brother, don't you think? While I am willing to believe that you harbor no ill will, I dare not ignore the possibility that you're a part of his plans.
Nor do I dare assume that I can beat him in on the battlefield of political intrigue.
Is my brother... really that odious a person to everyone else?
I can tolerate his scheming, but I cannot turn a blind eye to him trampling all over our traditions.
But not everything from outside is bad! Like, what if there were a better cure for Uncle Tarja's illness in some—

Ensia had only finished half her sentence when she sees the expression on Arctosz's face. She realizes then that a single gesture of aid from the patriarch of the Paleroche clan does not mean she has shortened the distance between them.
I can see that you and your brother are completely different kinds of people.
But both of you are true Silverashes.
Doesn't that also make you a true Paleroche?
Ah, of course.
But you're still helping me.
Do you think I should have sentenced Tarja to death, or continued to detain you?
No, no, that's not what I meant!
I just... don't quite understand.
Then keep mulling it over. You still have a long life ahead of you.
Let's go.
Hold onto your own stuff. You were so excited to leave that you forgot your bag.
Is that you, Lady Ensia?
Weiss? It's me! Over here!
I was worried sick about you—
Promise me you'll never do something that risky ever again!
But I'm perfectly fine, aren't I? The tearstone got delivered in time to boot. Maybe I ran into a snag or two along the way, but all's well that ends well.
Ugh... You're just as stubborn as the Master.
Hehe.
By the way, you may not know this, but part of the reason he left the country this time was to develop tearstone as a resource.
How so?
He'd already asked Victoria's scientists to study it earlier, and it turns out the reason tearstones can cure illnesses is because they contain a special substance.
And taking more or less from the cave at once does not change its efficacy.
If we can make an industry out of mining and refining tearstone, not only would that boost Kjerag's economy, but our medicine could also benefit people in other countries.
You won't have to risk your life to harvest it anymore.
Upon hearing Weiss's words, Ensia couldn't help but think back to what she saw in the cave.
The crystal-clear tearstones embedded in the rock wall, almost pulling her into a trance. As if they really were Kjeragandr's tears.
Twice had she plucked them from that wall for Uncle Tarja's sake, and the traces of her theft were left clearly in those vacant holes.
They mingle with dozens of other such scars, each of indeterminate age.
Ensia suddenly becomes uneasy, as if there were a conflict between her brother's development plans and the pristine beauty of the cave.
In an attempt to dispel some of her unease, she tries to change the topic.
By the way, what are we doing for dinner?
I heard Matterhorn mention that today's entrée will be braised beastmeat. I'm quite looking forward to it.
I didn't even realize I was hungry until now, but my stomach started growling as soon as you said that!
Glad to hear you have a healthy appetite. Anyway, I trust you'll sort out your mountaineering bag as usual, while I go help out in the kitchen?
Okay!
Oh Weiss, you joker...
This afternoon, you—
I was just about to thank you when you vanished without a trace before you could tell me your name!
Yet I arrived here all the same. Here, it's a letter for you.
For me?
From... my sister?!
Allow me to introduce myself. I am the Saintess's head maid, but you can call me Kjarr.
Enya's head maid?!
Could it be that she knew I'd be climbing the mountain today, and sent you to guide me?
As if. I was heading down to do some shopping and bumped into you by chance.
Then, you'd better not tell her that I climbed down the mountain in the snow!
Let's see here... I wonder how she's doing in the Vine-Bead Court...
Phew, sounds like it's going well.
By the way, Kjarr, thanks for delivering this! I'll tell Uncle Matterhorn to make dinner for—
Shh! I snuck in here.
Snuck in? But why?
Think about it. What would Weiss do if I graciously knocked on the front door, claiming to be the Saintess's head maid? He'd definitely report it to your brother.
From Enciodes's perspective, people from the Vine-Bead Court slipping down to bring you mail when he's not around is more than enough reason to go on high alert.
Oh...
Fair enough.
Anyway, I'll wait for him to return before I formally introduce myself to everyone in the family.
Gotcha.
Kjarr, this letter doesn't say anything about it, but Enya's still upset at him, right?
To be honest, yes, I believe so.
Do you think she'll end up siding with Mister Arctosz in the end?
You've known the Saintess much longer than I have, and should know far more about her place in the Silverash clan than I do.
She may be very upset at your brother, but you are still a sister to both of them.
Otherwise, you wouldn't be receiving this letter at all.
But she's now the Saintess of the Vine-Bead Court. Even if she wants to protect me, what can she do in our current situation...?
It's like how I had a run-in with Mister Arctosz today, and discovered that he's not a bad person at all.
No matter who they are, as long as they're involved in the struggle for power or profit, they'll always—
So that's what you're worried about.
Come. Let's cheer you up a bit first.
The Saintess's cheerful and optimistic little sister shouldn't be acting so gloomy.
Mm...
The Saintess is not someone who will allow herself to be led around by emotions. She knows better than anyone how much responsibility sits on her shoulders.
But the actions she ends up taking depend not only on your brother, but also on you.
You are not his tool. You have your own path to walk. Choose it, and you will definitely have an influence on them both.
I can't promise anything, but it's possible that the path you take will eventually form the bridge between them.
I see... I'm starting to get what you mean.
Then I'll be heading back. It's hard keeping away from Weiss's prying eyes.
So soon? I haven't even had a chance to properly thank you.
We'll being seeing each other a lot more in the future.
Bye for now, Ensia.
See you later, Kjarr!
Ensia watches the door close in front of her and sighs softly, before painstakingly folding the opened letter back up and stowing it in her pocket.
She then turns around and begins to organize her backpack.
Halfway through, she feels something strange inside her bag.
She digs around and places what she finds in front of her.
Two pieces of candy.
One is from the Paleroche clan's reception room.
She racks her brain hard to figure out where the other piece came from. Only then does she recall eating it once as a child. It was found only at the Vine-Bead Court.

recs.name: New Peaks
recs.tag: Cliffheart spends every waking moment thinking. What she can do for her brother and sister? And what can she do for Kjerag?

lines.x: Hah! One more!
Jump!
Safe!
That was a hard cliff.
Almost halfway to the top. I'll take a break here.
Is that... smoke? Why would someone start a fire out here in the middle of nowhere, in broad daylight to boot?
Could it be a distress signal?
Hard to gather firewood with my leg like this. Hope a hunter passes by and sees it...
Better be a human and not some wild beast...
Who's there?!
Don't worry, I'm just a mountain climber. I saw the smoke and thought it might be a distress signal.
Oh... thank goodness.
Someone actually came.
Is your leg hurt?
Yeah, I took a fall off a steep slope.
What's a Sankta doing on this mountain?
Ah, I'm from the Notarial Hall, and I'm executing a will of the deceased.
The instructions were to seek out a Sankta who left Laterano many years ago. I learned that he's living on one of these mountains.
I was searching around these parts, and, well... you can guess the rest.
The Notarial Hall sure works you hard, huh.
You know of the Notarial Hall?
Yeah. I'm with Rhodes Island. Have you heard of it?
Rhodes Island—ah, Federico.
My sympathies.
Haha. It's okay. We call him Executor, I think he's fun.
As long as you're not on a mission with him.
Could you help me get down the mountain?
I'll rest and recover in the town there before proceeding to execute the will.
You're continuing your mission?
Yes.
Alright, grab my hand.
So the Sankta came after all.
Samara, is it? I've been wondering... you Notarial Hall people seem just as busy as our operators, always on the move.
Why do you go so far for someone who left your city?
The law binds us, even if they've left Laterano.
The law...? You mean like in Kjeragandr?
Kjeragandr? Ah, you're from Kjerag, aren't you? I should have realized.
Yes, faith in Kjeragandr binds the people of Kjerag together.
Hm... there are subtle differences. From what I know, followers of Kjeragandr believe that Kjeragandr protects the people of Kjerag in subtle and mysterious ways.
For us, our faith is in the law of Laterano itself. We believe that there is a set of rules that binds us together.
We care for each other, understand each other, and hold ourselves accountable to each other.
That's how the Notarial Hall came to be, because we believe that all of us have a duty to do what we can for our people.
Kjeragandr's faithful care for each other too, but we're more subtle about it, because we believe that Kjeragandr has a plan for everything.
That's what you believe? Interesting.
This is my first real exposure to the Kjeragandr faith. I'd love to sit down and have a chat with you, if I had the time.
Unfortunately, I have a mission to complete, but thank you for helping me here, Ensia.
Once I've executed this will, maybe we could catch up—
Would you mind telling me more about the will? I might be able to help more.
Oh?
The mountains around here are steep, and dangerous for novice climbers. My mountaineering experience could be useful.
Of course, if it's classified or something, I won't push it.
Well, there's nothing particularly confidential about it.
Are you sure you want to do this, though?
It's no trouble. My field assignment is already done, and I've got some time before I have to return to base.
I wouldn't be climbing here otherwise.
In that case, I don't think I have the luxury of turning you down.
A renowned gun-knight, Reverend Regis, passed away recently.
In his will, he asked the Notarial Hall to find his brother, a scholar by the name of Legis, who left Laterano forty years ago after a rift between them.
A rift?
It occurred so long ago that it's unlikely anyone other than the two brothers know what happened. All we know is it had something to do with conflicting views on war.
His Holiness the Pope supported Reverend Regis's position, and Reverend Legis chose to go into exile.
Reverend Regis knew that Reverend Legis would not return to Laterano as long as he was there, so his hope was that Legis might return after his death.
If Reverend Legis is already...
He included instructions to bring back a token of Reverend Legis's, so that the brothers may be interred together.
To reunite a pair of estranged brothers...
I'm totally on board!
Any other details to go on?
I asked around and nobody had much contact with Reverend Legis, with the exception of a hunter by the name of Tiana.
I wasn't able to find her, so I started searching the nearby mountains.
A hunter?
Ah... that explains a lot.
Oh?
(Whisper) Maybe you didn't notice because you were injured, but we were followed.
(Whisper) What?!
(Whisper) I thought it was bandits looking for their mark, but now it seems likely it's the hunter you were talking about—
(Whisper) Head down.
Tsk.
Wait here.
I'll go after her!
Is there a signal here? Oh, thank goodness, I can reach one of the nearby nomadic cities.
Executor Samara reporting in. I need assistance.
Oh... Your Eminence?
She's a fast climber.
But I'm not too shabby myself!
Stop right there!
Hmph.
You're Tiana, aren't you?
Just a hunter passing by.
Drop the act. You wouldn't have tailed us for so long if you were just passing by.
You know why Samara is here.
You're Sarkaz?!
So what if I am?
Why would a Sarkaz—
Whoa—
You can move, I'll give you that.
Well, you sure can't shoot!
You think so?
(Wait, she's not aiming for me.)
(Could it be—!)
Too late.
Crap—!
Ouch—
Well, this is a deep pit.
You were luring me into a pit trap from the beginning, weren't you?
Not just that. I also saw how good you were at mountaineering and took your climbing gear.
The Sarkaz hunter pokes her head out and shows Cliffheart her backpack.
When did you...?
Don't worry, I'm not going to kill you. I'll go into town and tell them to send help.
I'll leave your backpack there. Once the rescuers arrive, take your stuff, and scram.
Why are you doing this?
My demands are simple.
Tell the Notarial Hall that Legis is not going back to Laterano.
I really should be more careful.
Ugh, this is a spiked cage...
Looks like it was a beast trap, the kind that poachers use.
But the spikes have been removed. I guess she really didn't want to kill me.
She probably removed them, in preparation for a day like this.
And in that case...
That Feline looks like she's tough enough to survive for a while.
I'll get the old man's stuff, then report to the town.
What a bother.
What?!
You left enough of the trap's mechanisms for me to climb out.
My hook's faster than your bow at this range.
Gah.
I just want to see Reverend Legis.
He doesn't want to see you. Get lost.
Take this, then!
Hmph—
Huh?
Look out! That rock isn't stable!
Wha—
Grab my hook!
Let go! I'm too heavy!
No!
I'm not leaving you behind!
If I can't pull you up... brace for impact!
Ghh—
Are you okay?
You should have let go.
You spared my life. One good turn for another.
That's not how it works.
I didn't mean anything by it when I mentioned you were Sarkaz. I was just surprised.
...I don't blame you. Anyone would be.
You might know that he has a brother—
Regis. Let me guess, he's dead, and now he wants his brother to go back to Laterano, is that it?
Yes.
He's not going back.
You're looking for him now? After so many decades?
It's Reverend Regis's last wish.
Plus, no matter how big their differences, settling these differences is what family is all about.
What makes you say that?
My brother and sister aren't on good terms.
B-But they're still siblings at the end of the day. All they need is the chance to open their hearts to each other.
You're trying to convince me when you don't even sound sure yourself.
Because if I give up, we'll never sit together again as a family.
And I know that, deep down, they care about each other.
There's nothing you can do.
Why's that?
Because...
Legis is dead.
*cough* Ugh, the dust.
I haven't been here since he died.
What was he to you?
I didn't know my parents. I was raised by a beggar in town. I guess you could call him my dad.
The townsfolk were okay, but no one was willing to take in a Sarkaz. I started to hunt for a living, after my dad died.
On one of those hunting trips, I ran into a big one and almost died. It was a passing Sankta who saved my life.
He shared some meat with me and told me I couldn't shoot worth a damn.
Ha.
I still remember... he froze for a moment when he saw me up close for the first time.
It took me a long time to realize it was because he realized I was Sarkaz, and thought about killing me.
But I was just a wild child who grew up in the middle of nowhere. I didn't know any of that.
I still don't really understand it, even now.
I had never seen a Sankta. I don't know why I should hate the halo heads. Plenty of worse people in town.
History is complicated.
Hey, that's what the old man said. I didn't take you for a scholar.
I'll take that as a compliment.
Well, I asked him to teach me how to shoot a bow.
But he didn't want me anywhere close. He chased me away with his gun whenever I went near.
It's funny, now that I think about it. He probably wanted to kill me many, many times, but I didn't get that. I thought it was all fun and games.
Maybe he got tired of chasing me away, but we eventually reached a kind of understanding. I would hide near his house, and he would show a move or two, pretending not to notice me.
What happened to him?
A bunch of Sarkaz bandits came three years ago. They tried to recruit me when they saw I was Sarkaz and could handle myself.
When I refused, they kidnapped me and tried to coerce me into joining.
The old man came to rescue me alone. I survived. He didn't.
...I'm sorry.
He never considered me his student. I don't think he would've wanted a Sarkaz student.
Without the skills I learned from him, though, I would have been dead long ago.
He never left this place, and no one ever came to look for him.
Now, his brother wants him to go back to Laterano? No way, not even if it's just his stuff.
He doesn't belong to Laterano. He belongs to this place.
Give up and leave, if you get it. Or you can die here.
Can I take a look around?
Suit yourself.
What are these books?
The old man liked to read. He tried to teach me, but gave up when he realized I was hopeless at it.
Histories of the Sarkaz and Sankta...
A lot of notes and annotations...
Hm? There's a piece of paper here.
A letter?

lines.st: Dear Regis. It is precisely because we were brothers that we were never able to come to a compromise through our empathy, for it would be insult to one another.
Was leaving the only option, though? Thinking back on it, perhaps there was a better way.
But we should not regret our choices.
Just because we made a choice does not mean the path not taken has lost its meaning.
That was why I chose to leave Laterano.
I do not think I shall ever return.
I will miss your strawberry milkshakes, though.

lines.x: Look at this, Tiana.
Legis didn't hold a grudge against Regis or Laterano.
He just made a choice, and chose not to return to Laterano because of it.
So what?
Either way, he doesn't want to go back to Laterano, does he?
It's not about going back to Laterano.
The brothers didn't have any bad blood towards one another. It's that simple.
People believe there is no conflict between the Sankta because they share emotions through empathy.
The reality is rather different. Sharing emotions may help you understand why the other side thinks a certain way, but it doesn't mean you must accept it.
On minor matters, the Sankta can certainly reach a compromise through empathy.
But there are certain things even the Sankta fail to agree upon.
The only consensus they can reach is that they do not agree.
Who are you?!
Velliv, Sanctae Lateranae Eccliesiae Cardinalis, Cardinal of the Holy Lateran Church.
Cardinal?!
Why—
Reverend Gun-knight Regis was highly respected. I happened to be visiting a nearby city, and when I heard there were difficulties executing his will, I felt it was my obligation to get involved.
I didn't expect someone else to take care of the problem before I could intervene, though.
No need to be nervous. I overheard your conversation from outside the door. It seems everything's been resolved with a nice little bow, yes?
Who told you—
The split between the gun-knight Regis and his brother, the scholar Legis, occurred over their attitude towards war.
Velliv raises her gun and points it at the Sarkaz.
Bitch.
I won't let you have your way, Sankta!
Tiana returns the favor, pointing her crossbow at the Sankta.
Reverend Regis and His Holiness approached war with a moderate attitude, while Reverend Legis believed in one that was more proactive and radical.
That was the cause of the split between us.
In his will, Reverend Regis requested the return of Reverend Legis's personal effects, in the event that Reverend Legis became deceased.
Those effects do not include a Sarkaz.
Wait!
This is no business for a mountaineer.
I can ask Rhodes Island to take her in!
If I recall correctly, Rhodes Island has a policy against interfering with a country's internal affairs.
The extent to which that policy is followed is debatable, but I doubt they would want to get involved in this one.
I... I can send her to Kjerag!
Kjerag?
I hope you understand the effect that deploying the Silverash name here will have, Ensia, my child.
You knew who I was from the very beginning, didn't you?
I won't deny it.
If you know my family name, then you also know my siblings.
Enya, Saintess of the Vine-Bead Court. Enciodes, CEO of Karlan Trade. It's becoming difficult to find someone who wouldn't know them.
At the end of the day, though, just my brother and sister. My brother and sister who haven't sat down at the same table for a decade, because of a choice my brother made.
Deep down, I understand.
It's not that my brother and sister don't understand each other, same as these two brothers.
It's the opposite: They understand each other's position, and understand that it's not something they can move past. They understand there are certain things that only the other can do.
That's why they'll never go back to the way they were.
I get it, but I can't give up on the idea.
I just learned that there was a pair of Sankta brothers in the same boat.
They understood that there could be no understanding. They chose to part ways.
But they had each other in their hearts, all the way to the very end.
A touching tale, but what does it have to do with stopping me?
The understanding between my brother and sister isn't about simple acceptance of the other's actions.
The most important thing is that they believe there is something about the other's choice that's correct.
They believe that their choice can affect the other.
Most importantly, when all is said and done, they'll stand at the same goal line.
A fine speech, Ensia.
Velliv lowers her gun.
Why you—
I was just planning to scare you away and let you go. After all, I can't very well let a Sarkaz cross my line of sight and do nothing about it.
But if Ensia has a better plan, I'm happy to go along.
You were sure you would win and planned to spare my life from the beginning?
Did you think otherwise? Consider it an act of magnanimity, even if it might be a little hard to accept.
Sankta bitch...
As Ensia said, Reverend Regis didn't necessarily think that Reverend Legis was wrong.
However, right versus wrong has never been the only factor in anything.
I won't take it all, just a little token. A book, or some manuscripts. Is that acceptable?
...Suit yourself.
I should say, your sincerity was touching, Ensia my child.
You have strengthened my belief that, even though we follow different faiths and live in different environments, we still have much in common with respect to the problems we face.
I can agree with that.
I thought all Sankta were like Exusiai, but now I know there are all kinds of problems between Sankta too.
Understanding that is the first step to understanding Laterano.

I could give you a ride, if you want.

Oh?

Are you not planning to go back?
Not yet.

Maybe they've already sat down together while I've been away.

Then I should cast my eyes forward, too.

I'll be the catalyst.
Kjerag is certainly in need of cultural dialogue, and there is no doubt that His Holiness will welcome such dialogue with open arms.
But I must ask you again, one last time.
Do you understand what you're doing, Lady Ensia Silverash?
Yes.
In that case, I welcome you on behalf of Laterano.
Thanks.
Oh, but I'll need to visit the nearest Rhodes Island branch office first.
I'll need them to help me find a home for Tiana, and ask the Doctor to deliver a message to my brother.
